result:
I found no issues in PR #1 that I'm confident are real bugs, so the finding list is empty.

What I checked:

- **Every path into the drain wait:** `stream_close()` now waits on the old `_outgoing_queue_ready` (`src/rpc/rpc.cc:562`). Frames that `send()` accepted before `_stream_closing` was set are written before the buffer is closed. Withdrawn entries and failed entries still resolve that wait. If `stop_send_loop()` runs at the same time, it is still serialized through `_sink_closed_future`.
- **Hangs before negotiation:** the wait could hang if `stream_close()` ran before negotiation finished. On the server a stream is only registered after negotiation. On the client, `sink::close()` runs `close_sink()` only after the eof `send()` resolves, and that send waits for negotiation itself. I found no way in.
- **Back-pressure:** a peer that stops reading can stall the drain. That is the same as before, since the old `write_buf.close()` blocked the same way.
- **The new flag:** it is only set on stream connections, and only once, because of the `!error()` guard.

One thing I couldn't settle: the new test asserts `client_factory.hooks.size() == 2` before any data has gone over the stream (`tests/unit/rpc_test.cc`). That assumes the client-side stream connection has already negotiated when `call(...)` returns. I didn't confirm that ordering is guaranteed, so the check could be flaky, but I'm not confident enough to call it a bug.
